subject: Request for SLA carve-out for customer-owned edge routers
messages:
From: Grace Lin <grace.lin@lumentech.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aaron Blake <aaron.blake@lumentech.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Oct 2028 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment SLA — customer-owned edge devices causing latency spikes

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We’re moving toward a private deployment in our Phoenix colo but we’ve run into an operational constraint that affects Redwood’s standard latency SLA. A subset of our site traffic traverses customer-managed edge routers (managed by our facilities team and a third-party carrier). Over the last 90 days we’ve seen intermittent 200–800ms spikes for ~1–2% of requests that correlate with maintenance windows and carrier route flaps.

We understand Redwood’s SLOs are built end-to-end, but in this layout LumenTech controls the last-mile switching/peering that creates measurable tail latency. We need to ask whether Redwood can accept an SLA carve-out for latency incidents attributable to infrastructure that LumenTech owns and operates, and if so what evidence you would require for attribution (packet captures, edge monitoring, timestamps, BGP updates, etc.).

Attached: phoenix-edge-topology.pdf (simple diagram), a short sample of our edge monitoring export.

High-level asks:
- Can we add an appendix that excludes customer-controlled edge and carrier peering jitter from Redwood’s latency SLA?
- What telemetry and runbook steps would Redwood require to validate an incident as customer-controlled?
- Are there specific language or ops commitments you’d want from LumenTech to make this carve-out acceptable?

We’d prefer a concise 1‑page appendix we can attach to the Private deployment order. Can you let us know next steps and whether this is something your ops/legal can accept in principle?

Thanks,
Grace Lin
Sr. Infrastructure Manager, LumenTech Medical
grace.lin@lumentech.com
+1 602-555-0134

Attachments: phoenix-edge-topology.pdf (diagram), edge-monitoring-sample.csv (CSV excerpt)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace Lin <grace.lin@lumentech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Oct 2028 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private deployment SLA — customer-owned edge devices causing latency spikes

Hi Grace — thanks for the clear summary and the diagram. We can absolutely consider a narrowly scoped SLA appendix that recognizes "customer-controlled edge/carrier peering" as an attribution class. That said, we need concrete telemetry and a deterministic attribution process to avoid opening an operational gap.

What Redwood would need up front (high level):
- A topology and list of ASN/peering points (you already sent a start).
- Time-synced monitoring: packet-level or jitter/latency samples with timestamps (NTP/ptp sync) for a 72-hour window around an incident.
- A runbook for your outage classification that shows who in LumenTech/your carrier will validate an event and share evidence.
- Optional: a BGP update history when available.

Operationally, we propose:
1) An appendix that excludes "customer-controlled edge and carrier peering" from Redwood latency SLOs, but only for incidents where LumenTech provides the above evidence and follows a joint incident validation process within 72 hours.
2) A requirement that the LumenTech on-call open a ticket in our joint portal and attach the monitoring/BGP evidence. Without that evidence, the incident will remain within Redwood SLO scope.
3) A periodic (quarterly) review of incident attributions and sample-synced telemetry to ensure the carve-out isn’t abused.

If you’re okay with that direction, I’ll loop in Legal to draft a tight one-page appendix and Ops to add the telemetry checklist. Karthik/Soojin — can you confirm the minimum evidence set we should require and whether the 72-hour validation window is feasible operationally?

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
VP, Customer Operations | Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Fwd: Private deployment SLA — customer-owned edge routers — fronting for attr policy

Folks — forwarding Grace's ask. My read: acceptable in principle but we need defensible evidence and tight wording. Proposed internal bullets to land with Legal/Contracts: 

- Keep appendix narrowly scoped to latency/uptime attribution for customer-owned edge/carrier peering only; do not widen to internal app issues.
- Evidence minimum: synchronized latency traces (NTP-synced), traceroutes from both sides, carrier maintenance logs, and BGP table deltas. Prefer CSV sample + PCAP when available.
- Validation process: LumenTech opens joint ticket, attaches evidence, Redwood has 72 hours to review/accept or request additional info; after acceptance the incident is classified as "customer-controlled" and excluded from SLO calculations.
- Quarterly audit: sample 5 incidents/quarter with mutually agreed telemetry. Exceptions to the evidence process should be escalated to Ops leadership.

Legal will want precise definitions of "customer-controlled edge" and "carrier peering" and a clause that Redwood may reclassify repeated attribution failures as service-impacting until evidence improves. Also suggest including an explicit data sharing and retention window (we should request 90 days of monitoring exports on request).

Karthik — can you confirm ops can do a 72-hour triage and sign off? Soojin — any red flags from the SRE/playbook side (e.g., minimum sample rates we should require)?

Thanks,
Evelyn
